label: input v at early original positions (t=0..3)
explanation: Fires when the input token is v during the original phase at positions 0-3. It does not fire on v at position 4 or later, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (aside from ~165 weak activations at t=5). Position sets the magnitude. t=1 gives the highest values (~1.0 of max, e.g. i [v] ...), then t=2 (~0.7-0.8) and t=0 (~0.4). t=3 is weak (~0.05-0.2) and is where most of the predicate's few false positives fall. A repeated v gives smaller or no activation.

issues: None of the claims are wrong. A few small details are worth recording.

Position split (dev): t=0, t=1 and t=2 each have precision 1.0. t=3 has precision 0.863 and carries only 5.6% of the activation mass. t=4 has precision 0.0 on 13867 v steps. This matches the claimed cutoff and the weak firing at t=3.

The t=3 false positives look like weak activations falling below threshold, not a structured class. Precision is flat across L=4..9 (0.853-0.871). Splitting on whether the previous token is a digit or a letter changes little (0.82 vs 0.87). Restricting to in_first only slightly raises precision (0.885).

The 165 copy-phase activations (171 misses on test, 0.0% of mass) all occur at t=5 in L=3 sequences (recall_idx=2), where the fed-back input is v. Their values are about 0.06-0.18. Even there, a copy-phase v with L=3 is active only 19% of the time. This is negligible.
'A repeated v gives smaller or no activation' is only partly true. Non-first v at t<=3 still fires 83.5% of the time, so 'often weaker' would be more accurate.
On the test split, precision 0.966, recall 0.997, F1 0.981 and mass recall 0.9995 match the reported scores.
